To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the space complexities of Chandy-Missa, Time Warp and sequential simulation are different; (2) the memory consumption of Time Warp is never less than that of sequential simulation; (3) an optimal Time Warp algorithm, cancelback, has been developed; (4) cancelback has a number of problems that must be addressed in its implementation; (5) an efficient implementation of cancelback, artifical rollback, is proposed.

Time Warp consumes at least as much memory as sequential simulation, Chady-Misra may or may not consume more memory than sequential simulation, and we have designed an optimal memory management protocol for Time Warp.
Time Warp simulation can be made optimal by cancelback, and artificial rollback can be used to reduce the implementation complexity of cancelback.
